तालमा तरबार नचाउँदै ‘वाख्खै… वाख्खै…’ को लयमा झुमेका स्थानीयले पुस्तौँ पुरानो सांस्कृतिक परम्परालाई फेरि एकपटक जीवन्त बनाए । विशेषगरी युवादेखि वृद्धसम्मको सामूहिक सहभागिताले पुण्यखोलाको फाँटलाई सांस्कृतिक उत्सवमा परिणत गर्‍यो । डल्ले सरायँ मेला मनोरञ्जन र रमाइलोको अवसर मात्र होइन, प्यूठानको ऐतिहासिक स्मृति, लोकविश्वास र मौलिक सांस्कृतिक पहिचानसँग जोडिएको पर्व हो । यसको सुरुआतबारे स्थानीय समाजमा विभिन्न किंवदन्ती प्रचलित छन् । स्थानीय बुढापाकाहरूका अनुसार भित्रिकोटका तत्कालीन अलोकप्रिय राजालाई स्थानीयले पदच्युत गरी डल्लेको फाँटमा ल्याएर मारेपछि त्यसको खुसीयालीमा तरबार नचाउँदै ‘वाख्खै’ भनेर उत्सव मनाउने परम्परा सुरु भएको हो । त्यही ऐतिहासिक घटनाको स्मरणमा सुरु भएको सरायँ नाच कालान्तरमा सामूहिक सांस्कृतिक उत्सवका रूपमा विकसित भएको स्थानीयको भनाइ छ । पुस्तौँदेखि हस्तान्तरण हुँदै आएको यो परम्पराले स्थानीय समुदायबीचको एकता, साहस र सामूहिक भावनालाई समेत अभिव्यक्त गर्दै आएको छ । डल्ले सरायँ मेलाको अर्को विशेषता यसको निरन्तरता हो । देशमा संकटकाल लागू भएका बेला र सशस्त्र द्वन्द्व उत्कर्षमा पुगेको समयमा समेत यो मेला रोकिएन । गाउँलेहरूले कठिन परिस्थितिमा पनि परम्परालाई निरन्तरता दिँदै आएको प्यूठान नगरपालिकाका उपप्रमुख देवेन्द्र बर्मा बताउँछन् । ‘भित्रिकोटका अलोकप्रिय राजालाई स्थानीयले पदच्युत गरी डल्लेको फाँटमा ल्याएर मारेको खुसीयालीमा वाख्खै भन्दै तरबार नचाएर सरायँ मेला गर्ने गरिएको बुढापाकाहरू बताउँछन् । देशमा सङ्कटकाल हुँदा र सशस्त्र द्वन्द्वका समयमा पनि यहाँको सरायँ मेला कहिल्यै रोकिएन’, उनले भने । मेलामा गाउँका दिदीबहिनीले सहभागी पुरुषलाई फूलमाला लगाइदिने परम्परा छ । फूलमाला पहिरिएका युवा तथा अधबैंसे पुरुषहरू हातमा तरबार लिएर परम्परागत भाकामा नाच प्रस्तुत गर्छन् । ढोल र मादलको ताल, सामूहिक नृत्य र ‘वाख्खै’ को गुञ्जनले मेलाको रौनक थप्छ । यसमा स्थानीय भेषभूषा र मौलिक शैलीको समेत विशेष महत्व रहने गरेको छ । ऐतिहासिक लिखित अभिलेख पर्याप्त नभए पनि स्थानीय लोकश्रुतिअनुसार डल्ले सरायँ नाच तेह्रौँ शताब्दीको अन्त्यतिरदेखि प्रचलनमा रहेको मानिन्छ । पछिल्लो समय यसको संरक्षण र प्रवर्द्धनका लागि प्रतियोगितात्मक रूपमा समेत सञ्चालन गर्न थालिएको छ । विसं २०७० देखि सुरु भएको प्रतियोगितामा यस वर्ष सात समूहले सहभागिता जनाएका थिए । प्रतियोगितामा खैरा समूह प्रथम, सापडाँडा समूह द्वितीय र पाण्डेडाँडा सरायँ समूह तृतीय भए । प्यूठान नगरपालिकाले प्रथम हुने समूहलाई एक लाख, द्वितीयलाई ७५ हजार र तृतीयलाई ५० हजार रुपियाँ पुरस्कार प्रदान गरेको छ । प्रतियोगितामा सहभागी अन्य समूहलाई पनि प्रोत्साहनस्वरूप २० हजार रुपियाँका दरले पुरस्कार दिइएको नगरपालिकाका प्रवक्ता एवं वडा नं. ४ का अध्यक्ष सुमनराज श्रेष्ठले जानकारी दिए । नगरपालिकाले डल्ले सरायँ नाचको संरक्षण र प्रवर्द्धनका लागि वार्षिक पाँच लाख रुपियाँ बजेट विनियोजन गर्दै आएको छ । यसलाई स्थानीय पाठ्यक्रममा समेत समावेश गरिएको छ । नगरपालिकाले डल्ले सरायँलाई सांस्कृतिक पर्यटनको आकर्षणका रूपमा विकास गर्ने नीति लिएको श्रेष्ठले बताए । स्थानीय संस्कृति र इतिहास बोकेको यस्ता परम्पराको संरक्षणमा पछिल्लो पुस्ताको सहभागितालाई महत्वपूर्ण मानिएको छ । आधुनिक मनोरञ्जनका माध्यम बढ्दै गएको अवस्थामा पनि पुस्तौँ पुरानो सरायँ नाचमा युवाहरूको आकर्षण कायम रहनुले यसको भविष्यप्रति आशा जगाएको छ । भाइटीकाको भोलिपल्ट पुण्यखोलामा दिनभर गुञ्जिएको ‘वाख्खै… वाख्खै…’ साँझसँगै शान्त हुन्छ । तर, त्यो आवाजसँग जोडिएको इतिहास, सामूहिक उत्सव र सांस्कृतिक विरासत भने अर्को वर्षको प्रतीक्षामा रहन्छ । संकटकाल र सशस्त्र द्वन्द्वले समेत रोक्न नसकेको डल्ले सरायँ मेला प्यूठानको पहिचान जोगाउने जीवन्त सांस्कृतिक धरोहर बनेको छ । Rupandehi. The Dalle Sarayan Fair, held the day after Tihar's Bhai Tika at Punyakhola in Pyuthan, has concluded this year with traditional joy and cultural fervor. The locals, swaying to the rhythm of 'Baakhkhai...Baakhkhai...' without swinging their swords to the beat of drums and madal, once again brought the age-old cultural tradition to life. The mass participation, especially from the young to the old, transformed the Punyakhola plain into a cultural festival. Dalle Sarayan Mela is not only an opportunity for entertainment and fun, but also a festival linked to the historical memory, folk beliefs and original cultural identity of Pyuthan. Various legends are prevalent in the local society about its beginning. According to local elders, the tradition of celebrating the festival without waving swords began after the then unpopular king of Bhitrikot was deposed by the locals and brought to the Dalle field and killed. Locals say that the Sarayan Dance, which began in memory of that historical event, has evolved into a collective cultural celebration over time. This tradition, which has been passed down for generations, has also expressed unity, courage, and a sense of community among the local community. Another feature of the Dalle Sarayan Mela is its continuity. This fair did not stop even when the country was under a state of emergency and the armed conflict was at its peak. The villagers have been continuing the tradition even in difficult circumstances, says Devendra Barma, deputy mayor of Pyuthan Municipality. "Elderly people say that the Sarai Mela was held without using swords, in celebration of the unpopular king of Vikhrikot who was deposed by the locals and brought to Dalle field and killed. Even during times of crisis and armed conflict in the country, the Sarai Mela here never stopped," he said. There is a tradition of village sisters garlanding the male participants in the fair. Young and middle-aged men wearing garlands perform traditional dances with swords in their hands. The rhythm of drums and madals, group dances, and the sound of 'bakkhai' add to the charm of the fair. Local costumes and original styles also have special importance in this. Although there are not enough historical written records, according to local folklore, Dalle Sarayan dance is believed to have been in practice since the end of the 13th century. Recently, a competition has been started to preserve and promote it. Seven groups participated in the competition, which began in 2070 BS, this year. In the competition, Khaira group came first, Pahanda group came second and Pandedanda Sarayan group came third. Pyuthan Municipality has awarded Rs 100,000 to the first place group, Rs 75,000 to the second place group and Rs 50,000 to the third place group. Other groups participating in the competition have also been awarded Rs 20,000 as an incentive, informed Suman Raj Shrestha, spokesperson of the municipality and chairman of Ward No. 4. The municipality has been allocating a budget of Rs. 500,000 annually for the preservation and promotion of Dalle Sarayan dance. It has also been included in the local curriculum. Shrestha said that the municipality has adopted a policy of developing Dalle Sarayan as a cultural tourism attraction. The participation of the next generation is considered important in preserving such traditions that carry local culture and history. Even with the rise of modern entertainment media, the continued attraction of the youth to the age-old Sarayan dance has raised hopes for its future. The day after Bhai Tika, the 'Baakhkhai...Baakhkhai...' that echoed throughout the day in Punyakhola calms down with the evening. However, the history, collective celebrations, and cultural heritage associated with that sound await the next year. The Dalle Sarayan Mela, which could not be stopped even by the crisis and armed conflict, has become a living cultural heritage that preserves the identity of Pyuthan.

The Dalle Sarayan Fair, held the day after Tihar's Bhai Tika at Punyakhola in Pyuthan, has concluded this year with traditional joy and cultural fervor. The locals, swaying to the rhythm of 'Baakhkhai...Baakhkhai...' without swinging their swords to the beat of drums and madal, once again brought the age-old cultural tradition to life. The mass participation, especially from the young to the old, transformed the Punyakhola plain into a cultural festival. Dalle Sarayan Mela is not only an opportunity for entertainment and fun, but also a festival linked to the historical memory, folk beliefs and original cultural identity of Pyuthan. Various legends are prevalent in the local society about its beginning. According to local elders, the tradition of celebrating the festival without waving swords began after the then unpopular king of Bhitrikot was deposed by the locals and brought to the Dalle field and killed. Locals say that the Sarayan Dance, which began in memory of that historical event, has evolved into a collective cultural celebration over time. This tradition, which has been passed down for generations, has also expressed unity, courage, and a sense of community among the local community. Another feature of the Dalle Sarayan Mela is its continuity. This fair did not stop even when the country was under a state of emergency and the armed conflict was at its peak. Young and middle-aged men wearing garlands perform traditional dances with swords in their hands. The rhythm of drums and madals, group dances, and the sound of 'bakkhai' add to the charm of the fair. Local costumes and original styles also have special importance in this. However, the history, collective celebrations, and cultural heritage associated with that sound await the next year. The Dalle Sarayan Fair, held the day after Tihar's Bhai Tika at Punyakhola in Pyuthan, has concluded this year with traditional joy and cultural fervor. The locals, swaying to the rhythm of 'Baakhkhai...Baakhkhai...' without swinging their swords to the beat of drums and madal, once again brought the age-old cultural tradition to life. The mass participation, especially from the young to the old, transformed the Punyakhola plain into a cultural festival. Dalle Sarayan Mela is not only an opportunity for entertainment and fun, but also a festival linked to the historical memory, folk beliefs and original cultural identity of Pyuthan. Various legends are prevalent in the local society about its beginning. According to local elders, the tradition of celebrating the festival without waving swords began after the then unpopular king of Bhitrikot was deposed by the locals and brought to the Dalle field and killed. Locals say that the Sarayan Dance, which began in memory of that historical event, has evolved into a collective cultural celebration over time. This tradition, which has been passed down for generations, has also expressed unity, courage, and a sense of community among the local community. Another feature of the Dalle Sarayan Mela is its continuity. This fair did not stop even when the country was under a state of emergency and the armed conflict was at its peak. The villagers have been continuing the tradition even in difficult circumstances, says Devendra Barma, deputy mayor of Pyuthan Municipality. "Elderly people say that the Sarai Mela was held without using swords, in celebration of the unpopular king of Vikhrikot who was deposed by the locals and brought to Dalle field and killed. Even during times of crisis and armed conflict in the country, the Sarai Mela here never stopped," he said. There is a tradition of village sisters garlanding the male participants in the fair. Young and middle-aged men wearing garlands perform traditional dances with swords in their hands. The rhythm of drums and madals, group dances, and the sound of 'bakkhai' add to the charm of the fair. Local costumes and original styles also have special importance in this. Although there are not enough historical written records, according to local folklore, Dalle Sarayan dance is believed to have been in practice since the end of the 13th century. Recently, a competition has been started to preserve and promote it. Seven groups participated in the competition, which began in 2070 BS, this year. In the competition, Khaira group came first, Pahanda group came second and Pandedanda Sarayan group came third. Pyuthan Municipality has awarded Rs 100,000 to the first place group, Rs 75,000 to the second place group and Rs 50,000 to the third place group. Other groups participating in the competition have also been awarded Rs 20,000 as an incentive, informed Suman Raj Shrestha, spokesperson of the municipality and chairman of Ward No. 4. The municipality has been allocating a budget of Rs. 500,000 annually for the preservation and promotion of Dalle Sarayan dance. It has also been included in the local curriculum. Shrestha said that the municipality has adopted a policy of developing Dalle Sarayan as a cultural tourism attraction. The participation of the next generation is considered important in preserving such traditions that carry local culture and history. Even with the rise of modern entertainment media, the continued attraction of the youth to the age-old Sarayan dance has raised hopes for its future. The day after Bhai Tika, the 'Baakhkhai...Baakhkhai...' that echoed throughout the day in Punyakhola calms down with the evening. However, the history, collective celebrations, and cultural heritage associated with that sound await the next year. The Dalle Sarayan Mela, which could not be stopped even by the crisis and armed conflict, has become a living cultural heritage that preserves the identity of Pyuthan.

Rupandehi. The Dalle Sarayan Fair, held the day after Tihar's Bhai Tika at Punyakhola in Pyuthan, has concluded this year with traditional joy and cultural fervor. The locals, swaying to the rhythm of 'Baakhkhai...Baakhkhai...' without swinging their swords to the beat of drums and madal, once again brought the age-old cultural tradition to life. The mass participation, especially from the young to the old, transformed the Punyakhola plain into a cultural festival. Dalle Sarayan Mela is not only an opportunity for entertainment and fun, but also a festival linked to the historical memory, folk beliefs and original cultural identity of Pyuthan. Various legends are prevalent in the local society about its beginning. According to local elders, the tradition of celebrating the festival without waving swords began after the then unpopular king of Bhitrikot was deposed by the locals and brought to the Dalle field and killed. Locals say that the Sarayan Dance, which began in memory of that historical event, has evolved into a collective cultural celebration over time. This tradition, which has been passed down for generations, has also expressed unity, courage, and a sense of community among the local community. Another feature of the Dalle Sarayan Mela is its continuity. This fair did not stop even when the country was under a state of emergency and the armed conflict was at its peak. The villagers have been continuing the tradition even in difficult circumstances, says Devendra Barma, deputy mayor of Pyuthan Municipality. "Elderly people say that the Sarai Mela was held without using swords, in celebration of the unpopular king of Vikhrikot who was deposed by the locals and brought to Dalle field and killed. Even during times of crisis and armed conflict in the country, the Sarai Mela here never stopped," he said. There is a tradition of village sisters garlanding the male participants in the fair. Young and middle-aged men wearing garlands perform traditional dances with swords in their hands. The rhythm of drums and madals, group dances, and the sound of 'bakkhai' add to the charm of the fair. Local costumes and original styles also have special importance in this. Although there are not enough historical written records, according to local folklore, Dalle Sarayan dance is believed to have been in practice since the end of the 13th century. Recently, a competition has been started to preserve and promote it. Seven groups participated in the competition, which began in 2070 BS, this year. In the competition, Khaira group came first, Pahanda group came second and Pandedanda Sarayan group came third. Pyuthan Municipality has awarded Rs 100,000 to the first place group, Rs 75,000 to the second place group and Rs 50,000 to the third place group. Other groups participating in the competition have also been awarded Rs 20,000 as an incentive, informed Suman Raj Shrestha, spokesperson of the municipality and chairman of Ward No. 4. The municipality has been allocating a budget of Rs. 500,000 annually for the preservation and promotion of Dalle Sarayan dance. It has also been included in the local curriculum. Shrestha said that the municipality has adopted a policy of developing Dalle Sarayan as a cultural tourism attraction. The participation of the next generation is considered important in preserving such traditions that carry local culture and history. Even with the rise of modern entertainment media, the continued attraction of the youth to the age-old Sarayan dance has raised hopes for its future. The day after Bhai Tika, the 'Baakhkhai...Baakhkhai...' that echoed throughout the day in Punyakhola calms down with the evening. Rupandehi. The Dalle Sarayan Fair, held the day after Tihar's Bhai Tika at Punyakhola in Pyuthan, has concluded this year with traditional joy and cultural fervor.

The locals, swaying to the rhythm of 'Baakhkhai...Baakhkhai...' without swinging their swords to the beat of drums and madal, once again brought the age-old cultural tradition to life. The mass participation, especially from the young to the old, transformed the Punyakhola plain into a cultural festival.

Dalle Sarayan Mela is not only an opportunity for entertainment and fun, but also a festival linked to the historical memory, folk beliefs and original cultural identity of Pyuthan. Various legends are prevalent in the local society about its beginning. According to local elders, the tradition of celebrating the festival without waving swords began after the then unpopular king of Bhitrikot was deposed by the locals and brought to the Dalle field and killed.
